findings.summary: Five differentiated driver-capability proof fields (executable_identity, permitted_auth_mode, observable_subscription_backed_usability, content_free_operation, tool_mcp_closure) plus approved_data_boundary were implemented for both mandatory drivers (claude, codex) in runtime/run_curriculum.py (_prove_one_driver/_prove_driver_capabilities), wired into both --preflight and the live --unit/--all/--resume path (_prove_live_capabilities), and consumed inside the compiled graph's own D03_PROVE_CAPABILITIES gate. N20's D03 tool/MCP-closure functions (transport.prove_claude_tool_closure/require_claude_tool_closure) are now genuinely called from real production dispatch, not left standalone. A permanent regression test reproduces the exact Run 26 defect (binaries present, provider unauthenticated -> not ready) and a permanent regression test reproduces N20-F06 (an MCP server listed under --setting-sources "" but needs-auth -> still correctly evaluated as closed).

N30's own design initially checked a driver-level union of all its jobs' data_classes against egress.PROVIDER_DATA_CLASSES[provider] as part of approved_data_boundary. Live testing against the real job registry showed this produces a false conflict for the claude driver (M08_REPAIR_NAMED_WORKBOOK_DEFECT, provider=anthropic, legitimately declares data class frozen_workbook_artifacts, which egress.py only lists under openai). On reflection this was N30 overreaching: preflight explicitly takes no --authorization (spec 16), so it has no run-scoped AuthorizationRecord to evaluate a data class against -- that per-job, per-run authorization is egress.authorize_subprocess_transmission's job at real dispatch time, already covered by N20's own suite. approved_data_boundary was corrected to check only provider membership in egress.PROVIDERS (still read-only, no local reimplementation), which is the honest limit of what a driver-level, authorization-free preflight check can prove. Not routed to N20: this was N30's own design correction, not a defect in N20's code -- egress.py itself was never touched.

tests/runtime/test_run_curriculum.py::FreshRunWiringTests::test_fresh_unit_run_builds_the_graph_once_and_invokes_with_a_fresh_envelope (pre-existing, in N30's write set) used a fixture authorization of {"openai": ["manifest_unit_projection"]}; manifest_unit_projection is only a valid data class under "anthropic" in N20's already-migrated egress.PROVIDER_DATA_CLASSES, so AuthorizationRecord.__post_init__ genuinely rejects it. This is a stale test fixture left over from before N20's provider-class migration, independent of any change N30 made (reproduced against a clean N30 checkout with N20's current egress.py). Corrected the fixture to a valid openai data class (frozen_unit_artifacts) inside N30's own write-set file.

The first working version of D03's new driver-capability gate required transport_registry.driver_capability_proof unconditionally, which broke 41 tests in files outside N30's write set (test_plan26_unit_graph.py, test_plan26_workbook.py, test_plan26_adversarial.py, test_plan26_repair_acceptance.py -- all N40-owned or elsewhere) because those integration tests build their own minimal registry test doubles, unaware of this new attribute, to exercise unrelated graph topology/plumbing. Corrected: D03 now reads driver_capability_proof best-effort (skips gracefully when the registry does not expose it, the same optional-duck-typing treatment observe_executable already receives a few lines below), while runtime.run_curriculum._prove_live_capabilities became the actual, unconditional, hard stop -- it always populates this attribute on the real registry and raises tp.CapabilityProofFailed before compiled.invoke() is ever reached if any mandatory driver is not ready. Reran the full tests/ tree after the fix: 1291 passed, 2 skipped, 419 subtests passed, 1 failed -- the 1 remaining failure (test_plan26_prompt_graph_controller.py::test_passed_nodes_remain_admissible_after_harness_or_predecessor_change) is confirmed pre-existing and unrelated (reproduces identically on a clean checkout with none of N30's changes applied; it concerns Plan 26's own prompt-graph receipt store, node N10_DEPENDENCY_API, nothing in Run 27's scope).

Live-verified defect, outside N30's write-set authority: transport.observe_codex_identity cannot extract an executed model from the real, installed Codex CLI's actual --json exec event stream. Reproduced with N20's own unmodified transport.build_codex_argv/observe_codex_identity against the genuinely installed `codex` binary (codex-cli 0.147.0, evidence/N30_PREFLIGHT_EGRESS/04_live_driver_capability_proof.log): the real events are {"type":"thread.started",...}, {"type":"turn.started"}, {"type":"item.completed",...}, {"type":"turn.completed",...} -- none of which ever carries a "model" key on any event whose type is in transport._CODEX_IDENTITY_EVENTS, so observe_codex_identity always raises IdentityUnobservable for a live codex call. tests/runtime/test_plan26_transport.py's own observe_codex_identity tests only exercise a synthetic fixture shaped like the older msg-wrapped protocol ({"id":"0","msg":{"type":"session_configured",...}}), never the real installed CLI's actual output, so this gap was never caught by N20's suite. Consequence: N30's new, correctly-implemented observable_subscription_backed_usability field honestly and correctly reports the codex driver as not ready in this live environment (claude fully passes all five/six fields for real, evidence/04 above) -- this is N30 behaving correctly given N20's current transport.py, not an N30 defect, and was not patched here. Recommended owner: N20 (runtime/langgraph_factory/transport.py, observe_codex_identity / _CODEX_IDENTITY_EVENTS). This finding is why this result's outcome is BLOCKED rather than PASSED: per this node's own instructions, a defect outside N30's write-set authority is routed, not patched or worked around.
